successCriteria.description: ILeaveBalanceService exposes exactly five operations: getBalance, getAllBalances, initializeBalance, deductDays, and restoreDays — each with the parameter arity (employeeId, leaveTypeId, fiscalYear[, days]) specified in PLAN.md Phase 9.

initializeBalance derives totalEntitlement from the active leave policy's entitlementDays (looked up via ILeavePolicyService.getActivePolicy) and persists a balance with usedDays=0, pendingDays=0, status=ACTIVE, and the provided fiscalYear.
initializeBalance throws a typed NoActivePolicyError when no active policy exists for the given leaveTypeId, and does not attempt to create a balance.
deductDays throws a typed InsufficientBalanceError when totalEntitlement - usedDays - days < 0 and does not call the repository's increment operation.
deductDays atomically increments usedDays via the repository when sufficient balance exists and returns the updated LeaveBalance with recomputed remainingDays.
restoreDays atomically decrements usedDays via the repository and throws when the restore would drive usedDays below zero, without calling the decrement operation.
remainingDays is computed as totalEntitlement - usedDays at read time on every returned LeaveBalance and is never written to storage by any service or repository code path.
INotificationService exposes exactly four operations — notifyLeaveSubmitted, notifyLeaveApproved, notifyLeaveRejected, notifyLeaveCancelled — each accepting a LeaveRequestDTO and resolving to void.
Each notification method completes without throwing (resolves to void) and produces a console log line; notifyLeaveRejected uses rejectionReason ?? 'N/A' when the reason is absent.
The leave-balance barrel exports ILeaveBalanceService, LeaveBalanceService, and the three custom error classes; the notification barrel exports INotificationService and NotificationService.
Jest unit test files exist for both services with mocked repository/policy dependencies, covering the happy path, each typed-error branch, and the remainingDays invariant.

constraints: All database access in the leave-balance service must go through ILeaveBalanceRepository — no direct pool/SQL calls in service code (GP-001, HARNESS no-direct-db-outside-repository).
No use of the `any` type anywhere in the new service files or tests; use `unknown` with type guards or typed mocks (HARNESS no-any, strict tsconfig).

Cross-module imports must go through the module barrel (index.ts) only — the leave-balance service imports ILeavePolicyService from the leave-policy barrel, not from internal files (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).
Notification log output must contain only request identifiers, employee IDs, dates, and reasons — never passwords, tokens, PII, or financial data (GP-004).
No unhandled promise rejections: every async service method either returns a value or throws a typed error that callers can catch (GP-006).
Test files use the `.spec.ts` extension as explicitly requested by the task and already established by prior phases; jest.config.js matches both `.test.ts` and `.spec.ts` patterns.
outOfScope: Real email/SMS delivery — the notification service is a console-log stub; actual transport adapters are deferred to a later phase.
Leave-request orchestration (submit/approve/reject/cancel workflow), controller, and routes — Phase 10 scope; this phase only provides the balance and notification services it will consume.

Audit record creation for balance deduct/restore operations — the dependency map lists leave-balance → audit, but Phase 9 does not wire audit writes; that integration belongs to the orchestrating leave-request service in Phase 10.

Balance status transitions (ACTIVE → EXHAUSTED → FROZEN) and pendingDays manipulation — Phase 9 implements deduct/restore of usedDays only; status lifecycle and pending-day reservation are not part of this phase.
HTTP routes, controllers, RBAC middleware, and input validation at API boundaries — no API surface is introduced in this phase (GP-003/GP-005 apply at the controller layer, deferred to Phase 10).

entityInvariants.invariant: remainingDays is a derived value equal to totalEntitlement - usedDays, computed at read time; it is never persisted or directly written by any code path.
usedDays must never become negative: deductDays rejects when the deduction would drive remaining below zero, and restoreDays rejects when the restore would drive usedDays below zero.
A newly initialized balance always has usedDays=0, pendingDays=0, status=ACTIVE, and totalEntitlement sourced from the active LeavePolicy.entitlementDays for that leaveTypeId.
Each balance is uniquely scoped by (employeeId, leaveTypeId, fiscalYear); initializeBalance creates one balance per that triple, referencing the active policy's id as policyId.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws NoActivePolicyError (typed) when no active policy exists for the leaveTypeId; propagates repository create errors. Must not create a balance when the policy lookup fails.

Throws BalanceNotFoundError when no balance exists for the (employeeId, leaveTypeId, fiscalYear) triple or when the atomic increment returns null; throws InsufficientBalanceError (typed) when totalEntitlement - usedDays - days < 0, without invoking the increment operation.
Throws BalanceNotFoundError when no balance exists or the atomic decrement returns null; throws an Error when usedDays - days < 0, without invoking the decrement operation.
Returns the LeaveBalance or null when none exists; propagates repository errors.
Returns an array (possibly empty) of balances for the employee/fiscalYear; propagates repository errors.
Each method resolves to void and must not throw under normal operation; the stub logs to console and completes successfully.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service's remainingDays computation (totalEntitlement - usedDays) must match the repository's rowToLeaveBalance derivation exactly — both use the same formula with no pendingDays subtraction, despite the reconciled architecture listing remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays. The as-built formula (without pendingDays) is authoritative for this phase.

initializeBalance must obtain the active policy via ILeavePolicyService.getActivePolicy(leaveTypeId) and read totalEntitlement from LeavePolicy.entitlementDays — matching the field name declared in the leave-policy model and service interface.

The notification service must accept LeaveRequestDTO as defined in shared-types (including the optional rejectionReason field) — not a locally redeclared type — so the stub is wire-compatible with the DTO the leave-request orchestrator will pass in Phase 10.

The repository's create input type omits remainingDays (Omit<LeaveBalance, 'id' | 'createdAt' | 'updatedAt' | 'remainingDays'>); initializeBalance must not attempt to pass remainingDays to repository.create, consistent with the never-stored invariant.

integrationPoints.why: initializeBalance depends on the leave-policy service to resolve the active policy and derive totalEntitlement from entitlementDays; this is the cross-module dependency declared in the architecture dependency map (leave-balance → leave-policy).

The leave-balance service delegates all persistence (findByEmployeeAndType, findByEmployee, create, incrementUsedDays, decrementUsedDays) to the repository interface from Phase 4 — no direct DB access in the service.
The notification service consumes LeaveRequestDTO from shared-types so that the Phase 10 leave-request orchestrator can pass request data to the notification methods without adapter conversion.

Phase 10's leave-request orchestrator will consume ILeaveBalanceService (initializeBalance, deductDays, restoreDays) and INotificationService (all four notify methods) as constructor-injected dependencies; this phase establishes the contracts Phase 10 depends on.
